name: Aurelius
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Organize interview notes, code excerpts, and synthesize themes into findings

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Unlimited users, projects, notes, insights, documents and storage.
tiers.notes: Public rate is shown per month but billed yearly.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited users, projects, notes, insights, documents and storage plus advanced capabilities.
tiers.notes: Public rate is shown per month but billed yearly.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom security, service and procurement terms.

pricing.billingTerms: Annual prices are public; a monthly toggle exists, but exact month-to-month rates were not exposed in the checked page output. A 30-day trial is offered.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Aurelius, organize interview notes, code excerpts, and synthesize themes into findings. The hard boundary is research-specific tagging, collaboration, reporting, and import workflows, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Organize interview notes, code excerpts, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent view of synthesized research findings.
whatYouLose: research-specific tagging, collaboration, reporting, and import workflows
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Aurelius because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: CATMA
alternatives.desc: Collaborative text coding in a browser, built by academics and uninterested in your sales funnel.

facts.install: Use the free hosted web app, or run the CATMA Standalone Docker image with its bundled GitLab backend
facts.dataFormat: The public service stores projects in CATMA's server-side GitLab repositories; standalone/self-hosted deployments keep CATMA and GitLab data in Docker volumes, with exports available as text, TEI-XML, CSV and Git repositories
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a serious collaborative text-annotation system, but it lacks Aurelius's researcher-friendly interview repository, rapid synthesis workflow, and product-research reporting.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted app is easy, but private/offline use means running a large Docker container with an embedded GitLab service and managing its volumes and updates

alternatives.name: QualCoder
alternatives.desc: Serious interview coding, memos and theme reports on your desktop, with serious desktop-software vibes.

facts.install: Windows installer/portable EXE or unsigned macOS DMG; Linux commonly runs the Python source or an Ubuntu release binary
facts.engines: Optional AI uses a local multilingual E5 sentence encoder and configurable LLMs including OpenAI GPT-4-class models, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Ollama and Blablador
facts.dataFormat: Each project is a folder containing imported media and a data.qda SQLite database; AI mode adds an ai_data folder with chat SQLite data and a local vector store
facts.gapVsPaid: It supports rigorous coding and memos, but collaboration, interface polish, and quick conversion of interview evidence into stakeholder-ready findings trail Aurelius.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is platform packaging: Windows and macOS binaries are unsigned, while several Linux setups require Python source installation; VLC is also needed for audio/video coding

alternatives.name: Taguette
alternatives.desc: Code interview excerpts and export themes without recreating an enterprise research repository.

facts.install: Free hosted signup, Windows EXE or macOS DMG, Linux pip install, or Docker for a self-hosted multi-user server
facts.dataFormat: Desktop projects and documents live in one local taguette.sqlite3 database; self-hosting can use SQLite or another SQLAlchemy database, while the free hosted service stores data on its server and encrypted off-site backups
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles highlights and themes well, but its text-focused scope lacks Aurelius's richer research repository, synthesis aids, and polished findings workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows and macOS packages install cleanly but are unsigned; Linux needs Python plus Calibre, and collaboration requires a configured server or the hosted service

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Aurelius in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize interview notes, code excerpts, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent view of synthesized research findings.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
